boundaries: Artifact Type is not Artifact instance.
Artifact Type is not Schema alone.
Artifact Type registration is not semantic definition, validation, conformance, or admission.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines Artifact Type semantics only. It does not admit Artifact Type/v2, retrofit v1 registrations, validate an instance, or grant authority.

scope.applicability: The versioned contract that determines the admissible machine representation, semantic Definition bindings, generated human projection, validation surface, ownership, and claim ceiling for one artifact kind.
exclusions: A Definition of the artifact's subject meaning.
An admission decision, validator execution, or authority grant.

examples: Product Identity can bind Product plus Identity Carrier Definitions.
Method Binding can bind Method plus Identity Relation Definitions without inventing another global meaning.
domain_context.explanation: Artifact Type/v2 uses this Definition to require semantic Definition references for every new type registration while preserving the admitted v1 registrations by exact predecessor reference.

plain_language.explanation: An Artifact Type is the contract for a kind of file: what it means, which machine shape is canonical, how people see it, how it is checked, and what a passing check does not prove.

boundary_conditions: The Artifact Type and every artifact instance retain separate identities.
A schema constrains representation but cannot supply missing semantic meaning.
A candidate Definition reference may support candidate authoring but must be admitted before Artifact Type admission.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: T = (type_id, version, semantic_definition_refs, schema@digest, canonical_direction, projection_contract, validation_contract, owner_route, lifecycle, claim_ceiling); valid_new_registration(T) only if semantic_definition_refs(T) != empty; registered(T) =/=> admitted(T).
scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Artifact Type is a versioned contract T for one artifact kind. T binds at least one semantic Definition, a closed machine schema, canonical-source direction, deterministic human projection, validation rules, owner route, lifecycle posture, and claim ceiling. Registration of T neither defines its subject meaning nor admits T or any instance.

notation.meaning: One exact version of an Artifact Type contract.
The admitted or candidate Definition identities whose meanings T operationalizes without redefining them.

testable_conditions: Every new registration has at least one resolvable semantic Definition reference.
The canonical machine file and generated human projection are explicitly directional.
The schema, generator, owner, lifecycle, and claim ceiling are exact and inspectable.
